newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares plunge on inflation, politics.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares plunge on inflation, politics.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell sharply on Tuesday in day-long selling prompted by higher-than-expected inflation and further buoyed by political worries in the afternoon, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 lost 110 points, or 6.98 percent to close at 1,465, but rebounded slightly from a late low of 1,453.
Trade volume decreased further to 22.79 trillion lira from Monday's 26.36 trillion.
"Political uncertainties unnerved the market and caused sales to accelerate," said Ismet Palanli from Ar securities.

Bulent Ecevit, leader of the Democratic Left Party, Turkey's biggest leftist party said his party would file a censure motion against the Islamist-conservative coalition to preserve the secular democracy in the country.

Brokers said reported uneasiness in the coalition's conservative wing over last Friday's Islamist protest further irritated the market which was initially depressed by higher-than-expected inflation data at the opening.

Tanks and armoured personnel carriers on Tuesday paraded through Ankara's Islamist-controlled Sincan district, which staged an anti-Israel protest last Friday in an apparent show of strength by the staunchly secularist army.

Turkish wholesale prices rose 5.6 percent and consumer prices rose 5.9 percent in January, against 3.4 percent and 3.9 percent, respectively in December and earlier market predictions of between four and 5.3 percent.
The index had shed 3.62 percent in the morning session on poor inflation data, a continued consolidation as well as an approaching holiday, brokers said.

Cash drain from the market was anticipated in the first half of this week due to the Islamic Ramadan holiday in Turkish markets next Monday and Tuesday. Investors in Turkey usually seek repo deals on the bond market ahead of longer holidays.

"The market may rise on Thursday and Friday after some more selling for liquidity purposes tomorrow. But political developments will be watched closely now that the market is haunted by politics," Palanli said.
Brokers anticipate buying in the last two days of this week because settlements of transactions will be delayed until after the holiday.
The index has lost 13.82 percent since last Monday's all-time high close of 1,700 after surging 74.2 percent and hitting 17 record closes from end-1996 to January 27.

Of the 237 shares traded, falls outdid rises by 215 to nine and 13 closed steady. The IMKB Industrial lost 5.53 percent to 1,520, the IMKB Services dived 7.47 percent to 1,413 and the IMKB Financial plunged 7.85 percent to 1,433.

Leading actives were largely state-owned flat steel giant Eregli, down 1,000 lira at 21,000, T.Isbank's C series, down 2,000 lira at 30,000 and utility Cukurova Elektrik, down 22,500 lira at 210,000. They made up 27.7 percent of the total volume.
